rows.description: Section 16.5 'General Cap' definition changed from 12 months of fees to 3 months of fees.
Section 14.1 non-renewal notice window changed from 'at least 30 days' to 'at least 5 days'.
rows.beforeQuote: (b) either party notifies the other of non-renewal at least 30 days prior to the end of the current Subscription Term.
rows.afterQuote: (b) either party notifies the other of non-renewal at least 5 days prior to the end of the current Subscription Term.

rows.description: Section 5.1 automatic-renewal language removed; the agreement now ends at the end of the Subscription Period with no renewal.
rows.beforeQuote: For each Order Form, the Agreement will start on the Order Date, continue through the Subscription Period, and automatically renew for additional Subscription Periods unless one party gives notice of non-renewal to the other party before the Non-Renewal Notice Date.

rows.description: Inserted a new Section 1.8 'Exclusive Dealing' clause requiring Customer to use Provider as its sole software vendor for competing functionality. The original has only an unrelated non-exclusive license grant, which the Calder taxonomy explicitly excludes from this category.
rows.afterQuote: During the Subscription Period, Customer will use Provider as its sole and exclusive provider of software with substantially similar functionality to the Product, and Customer will not license, develop, or deploy any competing software from another vendor without Provider's prior written consent.

rows.description: Section 10 'Governing Law and Courts' removed entirely.
Inserted a new Section 5a creating an SLA-specific aggregate liability cap, written in plain language ('aggregate liability ... will not exceed') rather than Bonterms' defined-term style.
rows.afterQuote: **5a. Aggregate Liability.** Notwithstanding anything else in the Agreement, Provider's aggregate liability for all Service Credits and other claims arising out of or relating to this SLA will not exceed the amount of Fees paid by Customer for the affected Cloud Service in the three months preceding the claim.

rows.description: Section 11.2(b) 'Termination for Convenience' removed; only for-cause termination (Section 11.3) remains.
rows.beforeQuote:
11.1. Agreement. This Agreement starts on the **Effective Date** and continues until the end of all SOW Terms, unless sooner terminated in accordance with its terms. If no SOW Term is in effect, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason with notice to the other party.

11.2. Individual SOWs. (a) SOW Terms. Each SOW Term will be for the period specified in the SOW. (b) Termination for Convenience. Unless otherwise specified in the SOW, Customer may terminate any SOW for any or no reason at any time upon 30 days’ notice to Provider, provided that such termination will not become effective until Customer has paid all fees and expenses incurred through the time of termination.
rows.afterQuote: This Agreement starts on the **Effective Date** and continues until the end of all SOW Terms, unless sooner terminated in accordance with its terms. If no SOW Term is in effect, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason with notice to the other party.

rows.beforeQuote: During the term of the Agreement and for six months after, each party will carry commercial insurance policies with coverage limits that meet the relevant Insurance Minimums required in the SOW, if any. Upon request, each party will give the other a certificate of insurance evidencing its insurance policies that meet the required Insurance Minimums. A party's insurance policies will not be considered as evidence of its liability. Insurance coverage will be on a date of occurrence form and waive rights of subrogation or crossclaim.

rows.description: Inserted a new Section 6.4 'Warranty Duration' stating the warranty applies for 12 months from delivery. The original states a 45-day claim/cure procedure but never states how long the underlying warranty itself runs.
rows.afterQuote: The warranty in Section 6.3(c) applies for twelve (12) months from delivery of the Deliverables. Provider has no obligation under this warranty for issues reported after this period.

rows.description: Section 11 'General' consent-based assignment clause replaced with an unusual clause permitting free assignment to anyone, including a direct competitor, without notice or consent.

Section 9.3 'Customer Audit' removed entirely, along with the 9.2(c) cross-reference to it. Only Provider's unilateral sharing of its own audit reports remains — Customer has no right to initiate an audit or inspection.

Section 5.1 'Audit Rights' (which granted Customer the right to conduct audits, including inspections) replaced with a 'Compliance Reporting' clause that explicitly prohibits Customer from requesting an audit or inspection, substituting a periodic written questionnaire.
rows.beforeQuote: Audit Rights. Provider will give Customer all information reasonably necessary to demonstrate its compliance with this DPA and Provider will allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections by Customer, to assess Provider’s compliance with this DPA. However, Provider may restrict access to data or information if Customer’s access to the information would negatively impact Provider’s intellectual property rights, confidentiality obligations, or other obligations under Applicable Laws. Customer acknowledges and agrees that it will only exercise its audit rights under this DPA and any audit rights granted by Applicable Data Protection Laws by instructing Provider to comply with the reporting and due diligence requirements below. Provider will maintain records of its compliance with this DPA for 3 years after the DPA ends.
rows.afterQuote: Upon written request, Provider will give Customer, on a confidential basis, a summary copy of its then-current Report so that Customer can verify Provider’s compliance with the standards defined in the Security Policy.
